text: Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville should be ashamed of themselves. You would think that a company claiming to be the large dealer of classic automobiles would pride themselves on their products and customer service, not in my case however. I wanted to purchase a classic truck and using the internet came upon Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville website. On their website they provide links to view automobiles that they sell and the site also provide a description of the automobiles. I selected the link to view for a 1965 Chevy c-10 pick up truck. In the video the truck looked to be in pristine condition. The engine was running, both head lights working, no cracked windows....However, after purchasing the truck, I discovered otherwise. What I actually received from Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville was a truck that needed to be pushed off the lift and into my driveway. Because the engine did not start, I had to have it towed to a mechanic. After my mechanic looked over the truck, the following items were also discovered: the choke was broken, no speedometer cable, bad spark plugs, no horn, or working wiper switch, and the front brakes were worn down to almost nothing. Along with a broken driver side window and 1 head light not working... While it cost me $1300.00 to fix all the problems with the truck, I asked Dennis Severs, the sales manager for Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville to reimburse me, for the engine problem, cracked headlight and broken side window. At first he Mr. Severs deny there was a problem and blame it on "bad gas." After speaking with Brad Kline the Sales Manager of all Gateway Classic Cars showrooms, I was provided with no resolution. Instead their offer was $250.00 and I have to sign what they called their "standard release" which would prohibit me from writing this. First, let me say in my opinion, the pictures and video shown on Gateway Classic Cars website of the truck I purchased, did not provide a good resemblance of the truck that Gateway Classic Cars actually delivered to me. In my opinion, after viewing the truck up close, the paint was an average at best, (while the pictures on the website looked great). I will never purchase from them again. But if you are thinking about buying from them be very careful...

text: After spending forever looking for a room I finally found this place and it seemed decent so I booked it. Then I read the Yelp reviews and got nervous. Too many Yelpers have had run in with the manager and I find that (still) worrisome. However, my stay was uneventful in the best way possible and the price was great! Check in and check out were super easy and the staff was welcoming. The room had exposed brick wall, high ceilings, a ceiling fan, large, bright window into the courtyard, tv, microwave, free wifi that worked just fine, and a bathroom with new fixtures. The room was clean and cozy with a large and super comfy bed. My own gripe was that the only place in which I could plug in my phone was at the microwave where there was a power strip. There is a breakfast buffet in the courtyard which I suppose in cold weather wouldn't be much fun but given the layout, I don't see where else they would put it. Regardless, I was happy for some breakfast and hot coffee. I cannot complain about the noise. When I was in the bathroom I could easily hear my neighbors but once I went into the sleeping area I couldn't hear anyone. The building is old so of course it creeks and you can hear people walking around above your head. Big deal! You want to the Ritz, go stay there but I was happy in this historic building. I liked that I could walk right out of my room and find a bench and table in a quiet area in which to relax. The hotel is right near Walgreens and the trolly and it is in a nice, quiet area. I loved walking around the French Quarter all day and I was just as happy to come home to a quiet, cozy spot the sleep. I'm tempted to stay here again.

text: I love Bridgewater's and am surprised to see some of the negative reviews. I've been going for years. In some phases I might go a few times a month, and then not go again for months, but I am never disappointed. Sometimes I'm alone at the bar; other times at a table with one or two others. The regular bartenders are always good to great; the servers at the tables change around more but I've always found them to be totally fine to really good. Depending on your tastes I'd think you'd find the beer list super at best, fine at worst. I'm not so into all the German beers; that said, I always find something I like on draught and there are always other options to satisfy. As a vegetarian, I'm usually satisfied with the offerings. The menu changes somewhat but is consistently flavorful and satisfying. No, it's not dirt cheap bar food, but then, it's not cheap bar food, either. For these prices, if I thought the food was mediocre, I'd be pissed about it. But, that's not been my experience at Bridgewater's. Generally, I feel like the prices might be on the higher end of the standard bar range, but the value is decent and I never leave feeling resentful. In fact, as a regular train rider, I usually leave feeling incredibly thankful that we have such a great bar at our train station.

text: I could not be more disappointed that I am giving this place such a negative review. My first visit was an appointment with Dr. Rubin who was nice, calm, helpful, and everything her zocdoc reviews had said about her. However a few weeks afterwards I had tried to get a prescription changed and I ended up calling every day for two weeks until I finally heard back. I kept getting the same message "yes, she has been given her messages, she will get back to you." No estimated time frame. And after two weeks my prescription was nearly out. I had to call every hour until finally I heard back at the end of the day, the day before my script ran out. This is frankly irresponsible when it comes to medical concerns. And it is not just the administrative staff's fault. It is a lack of urgency of wanting things to change. During my first appointment, Dr. Rubin had discussed how she really wanted to build a good practice, where people keep coming back and building relationships with their doctors. It is impossible to trust a doctor I cannot get in touch with. Against my judgement, I went there again recently and the same experience. Yes it took an extra hour for Dr. Rubin to actually see me. This time was more rushed but still friendly and compassionate. However I've been trying to get results from a simple blood tests (taken next door to the practice) and I am running into the same issue. I have zero faith in their administration which is why I keep calling back every hour now. It should be a common practice to not make your patients wait once their test results come back. It is the most frustrating thing in the world when they have your test results and they can't find anybody who will read it back to you. Either hire a nurse, who's full time responsibilities include getting back to patients or have a specific time in your schedule when patients can expect to hear from you. This is not the way to run a medical practice. So I beg you, no matter how nice the doctors are, it is not worth the hassle. The word "unreliable" and things related to your health should not go hand in hand.

text: I had a furnace diagnosis done. $250. PROS: neat, clean, polite, on time CONS: expensive, pricing unclear, slow, charged labour rates to order parts and check on warranty, felt very sketchy. I hired this company based on reviews from homestars site but later discovered the site is not considered to be very reputable. I thought the cost was $109 for the diagnosis but that is the cost to show up. Then they charge $129 per hour labour. I wouldn't have hired then if I understood that. However, even though they were unclear, I thought the misunderstanding was reasonable (though disappointing). The tech took the entire hour to "diagnose" the problem with 20 minutes of that hour spent in his vehicle.....checking on the warranty coverage. I don't think that this is legitimate part of the labour fee. Certainly the company I eventually hired didn't charge me labour for those things. The second thing about the length of the diagnosis (exactly one hour), is that I knew what the problem was, I knew the error codes and told the tech. I needed the Hvac certified diagnosis to get the warranty. It's very simple issue to diagnose....I could appreciate that there are some standard best practices and extras to check to see if there maybe additional problems but it really shouldn't have taken more than 30 minutes at the absolute most (with all the extras)! The third thing I was disappointed about was I told the company before coming was that it was a warranty job and I wanted the job under warranty. I was VERY CLEAR about this. I mentioned it twice on the phone and once by email. They told me after they had completed the diagnosis and I had paid the bill that they would offset my bill by the warranty amount but wouldn't do the job for the amount provided under the warranty (100% parts and labour). To be fair, I dealt with three other companies and the warranty amount provided is less than market rates in Edmonton. One company even denied there was a warranty. It is not popular. The warranty company warned me about this and I warned First Call. If they had been up front and honest that they would charge me extra, I would not have hired them and I felt taken advantage of. It seemed dishonest to me to say you will accept warranty work but then charge the client extra. Fourth, I was rather aghast when the tech told me I should appreciate their willingness to offset the warranty because some companies will submit warranty claims without telling the homeowners and pocket it as profit.......whaaaaaaaattttt? I'm giving this place two stars rather than one because I think they may have been poorly represented by this employee. Their pricing is still higher than average but they are readily available. So if you need something done quickly, they can likely accommodate you without having to pay their overtime rate. I would suggest that you stay with them while working to insure you are charged for genuine labour. I would also make sure you agree up front that "truck time" is not "labour".

text: One of the best music venues in the USA. Not just Nashville, but America. They host bands that are 100% pure Bluegrass / Americana, not country music. You will find the very best musicians in the entire genre play here. Pretty much every soon-to-be great band plays here on their way up. We caught a young (early 20's) foursome called The Barefoot Movement. Un-freaking-believable. text: Food: ***** Service: * I own a restaurant so I am overly sympathetic and empathetic when I am not getting top notch service- maybe it was a slammed lunch and our server is worn out, whatever. But when the offenses start piling up my empathy dries up. That's what happened with my highly anticipated, partially disappointing visit to Cold Springs Tavern. As an out of towner with a love of barbecue I was on a mission to try California-style barbecue. I had only read about CA's tri-tip beef contribution to the food genre and I was stoked to learn about the secluded Cold Springs Tavern from a local gal pouring wine in a tasting room in Los Olivos. So my wife and I made plans to eat a late lunch there the following day (yesterday, a Saturday). We found it, parked and were seated in the back room at about 2:20, the last turn before the 3pm close of lunch service. The room was quiet and tucked back but full of a group at a six top and two other couples at the only other two tops. The room was right next to the server stand and the kitchen entrance. A young lady took our drink orders (water and wine for my wife, a beer for me) after cleaning the floor of some dipping sauce that she spilled on the floor. She brought my wife's wine and left, returning to bring something to the table where she had spilled the sauce. That couple asked her to clean the sauce that was still on their table cloth and dripping down the side. She probably didn't see it, no sweat. A guy server took our food order after answering our questions and steering us toward what we wanted- awesome. Our cup of wild game chili came out. But my beer was nowhere to be seen- nor the water. After a couple minutes and went out to find her and see what was up. She said they're out of it. Okay, would have been nice to know that. She offered an alternative but I could get it at home so I walked to the bar to see my options- the bartender mentioned another CA beer that I didn't remember from the menu that I wanted so I got it and went back to my seat. The chili was amazing. A different guy server brought our sandwiches- the tri-tip in sauce and the tri tip option with sauce on the side as well as apple horseradish and salsa. They were awesome. I preferred the undressed option with sauces on the side. I ended up not using much sauce and much preferred the salsa with some of the horseradish. My side of potato salad was not with mine- forgotten by the kitchen or our server or both. Good- I wanted to change to the regular chili. Our girl server had been in the server stand area texting on her phone but she was not in sight- I saw the bartender and asked her, so she brought the chili. It was also very good. My wife needed another glass of wine- and the water, it was a hot day. Eventually my wife got up and tracked down our drink server and asked for another glass of wine and the water. Things are starting to turn sour at this point. The girl brings the wine and water, sets it down and walks off, no "Here you go!" or "How is everything?" We wrap up, ask one of the guys at the server stand if we can get a to go box and our check. The room is empty at this point. It's quiet, no music, an unwelcome feeling from the drink server, and we are now talking not about how good the food is but how jacked up our service has been. The fella who took our food order brings the box and the check, asks how everything was. We said food was awesome but our girl server "needs some work". He said the servers don't have sections and everyone kind of works all tables. While we're boxing up the leftovers our drink server comes into the room to go through a closed door in the corner behind my wife's chair. She kicks the leg of my wife's chair and again doesn't say a thing. We are definitely getting bad energy from her now. I leave a ~10% tip on the credit card slip and take it to the bar so I can explain the low tip. The bartender is not around and our salty drink girl is behind the bar so I leave the slip on the bar and we leave. I'm writing all this for two reasons. First, to defend my low tip. My wife and I run two food service businesses, a lunch spot and a dinner restaurant. The servers were undoubtedly talking about us and the low tip when we left and this is my only way of explaining to them what went down. I am a 20%+ tipper- unless the train really goes off the tracks, which it did. Second, hopefully management reads Yelp reviews. I sure do. Maybe the no section thing usually works but for us it didn't. If our girl servers function is drinks, then she needs some training. She smiled- initially- but her communication was non-existent (except for whoever she was texting with). It was a downer of an experience and it colored my mood for the next few hours.

text: Zahav is one of the most well-received restaurants in all of Philadelphia, and for very good reason. My dinner there was one of the best I have ever had, so let me break it down for you. After some debate, my party of four opted for the Tayim option, wherein you get the Salatim salad plates and your choice of hummus to share, plus two mezzes (small plates), one Al Ha'esh (entree), and one dessert per person. At $42 a head it may seem expensive, but as soon as the food starts coming, you'll soon realize it was worth it. The Salatim consisted of six small plates: beets, cabbage, beans, eggplant, grape leaves, and carrots. All were packed with flavor profiles that belied their simplicity. I point out the eggplant and beets in particular as the highlights among this bunch. The hummus came out at around the same time, and we chose the Turkish style. This hummus plate changed how I will think of hummus forever. Never have I eaten hummus served warm before, and now to eat it cold is unthinkable to me. Just get it and thank me later. At this point in the meal, my friends and I were already fairly satiated, but the best was yet to come. The mezze plates came out two or three at a time, which was a perfect cadence for us to fawn over each dish. The Tayim dining option is most advantageous due to the selection of mezzes, which between the four of us meant we could try 8/13 possible mezzes. All of our choices came out flawless, in taste and composition. If I had to rank them, it would be: Tier 1: Fried Cauliflower, Crispy Haloumi, House Smoked Sable Tier 2: Chicken Freekah, Grilled Duck Hearts, Yemenite Beef Stew Tier 3: Kibbe Naya, Crispy Lamb's Tongue Let me try to describe the Crispy Haloumi for a second. The layers of flavor as you chew the haloumi over and over in your mouth slowly uncover, and your eyes grow ever so slightly larger with each bite. That is the experience of eating this dish. I could probably write a paragraph about each of the mezzes, but on to the entrees. My lamb merguez was very good, but I think my palate had taken a beating from the round of mezzes. However, I also sampled my friends' branzino and sirloin, both of which were sparkling. The sirloin in particular was juicy though cooked rare, a pleasant surprise as I usually prefer more cooked steak. To top it all off, dessert was the perfect way to end a night of indulgence. The pumpkin basboosa and coffee custard were both a delight. Zahav has received a lot of hype on this website and elsewhere, and I will say that every word is well deserved. With a well-balanced menu, wonderful service, and a generally welcoming atmosphere, there is no reason you should have reservations about making your next reservation Zahav. Book in advance!

text: I did it! NV Transformations works if you stick to the plan and lean on the great social media family for tips. I went through the orientation and was sneaking out the front door afterwards because this is a no excuse plan. I thought that there was no way that I could do this with a full time job and two kids under four. Luckily I bumped into a friend who made me realize I could do it as long as I pushed myself out of my comfort zone. I am so grateful I did not walk out the door that day because I am 22.8 lbs lighter in only six weeks. The workouts are five stars. I enjoy how every day is a different work out. There were even new moves I had never seen on my last workout of the six weeks. I appreciated that the coaches would provide modifications if needed. I am also a big fan of Zumba Dan. Coach Dan radiates positivity and confidence. His outlook is refreshing when you are sticking to the plan. One of the down things is that his class on Monday nights is in the small room and there are no real speakers. I love to dance and it is hard to get into it when the sound is clashing with the other room and the lights are full blast. It could also be that I was spoiled because I love the fact that in the main room workouts have lights go down and music goes up. It feels like a night club and it is a great change to the normal stale gyms. I felt that my challenge must have been one of the largest because the classes were pretty big. I am looking forward to the new location because that might mean a bit more personal attention will be available on how to improve or push myself. Don't get me wrong, when I asked for help I received it. I also appreciated that Eric made an effort to learn everyone's name even if he had to ask multiple times. The down side of the large classes was that I didn't really have "a coach." People on the facebook pages would refer to "their coach." To my knowledge I wasn't assigned to someone so I thought that I might have been missing out. It also seemed that the coaches rotated through classes so we had someone different typically. I also feel like there is an opportunity for clearer information when it comes to the meal plan. Much of the information that is needed is spread across three pages in the workbook and sometimes contradicts itself. I did not realize until the second week that I was not suppose to dip into the bottom bracket of food. I was also a bit unclear if I was to follow the weight on the portion sizes in the book or the palm, fist, cupped hands portions recommendations. I think I are way too much food the first week which made for a slow start. I did get great support from Jessica when I knew I was struggling with my meals. Overall, I would say that if you have tried everything, nothing worked, then this is what you need to do. It made me accountable for my own actions and has started some great habits why eliminating the bad ones. I signed up for another round to say the least.

One bowl had pretty tasty 5 spice ribs, but was on a "noodle veggie" salad that consisted of julienned cold, soggy vegetables dressed only in sesame oil, which were not tasty at all. The other bowl, a Moroccan meatball bowl, was uniformly terrible. The meatballs were way too sweet, soggy over cooked carrots were seasoned with only mint and were weird, and the cous cous was also overcooked (and kind of soupy - they had not been fully drained after cooking) and seasoned with too much saffron and no salt whatsoever. We could handle a few bites from that at most. A server came by and asked us how it was and we politely explained what we didn't like, and his response was "bummer". No apology, no offer to make it up to us in any way, nothing. I'd let a well intentioned local establishment like this slide for a bad food experience, but that lack of basic service was upsetting. text: Overrated. Unimaginative. And unnecessarily expensive. Come to this place if you like the idea of a pricey Mexican restaurant with a nice ambience. However, the food leaves much to be desired if you've ever been to other better Mexican restaurants in the area (there are many). My girlfriend and I both got the margaritas which were warm (even though they were "on the rocks") and barely had any tequila in it. And they were $12 each. We also got the chipotle guacamole with queso fresco. The cheese was in large blocks which made it tough to scoop with the nachos. The guac was okay. My gf got the empanada appetizer as an entree and those were pretty good, no complaints there. They were either baked or very lightly fried so the crust was nice and flaky. I ordered the seafood enchiladas. They were nice and cheesy. It had crab meat and shrimp. I didn't like it much but seafood isn't really my thing. I love enchiladas though so I thought I'd give it a try but was not so lucky. This was not the restaurants fault. What was their fault and what I found really strange was that the waiter forced us to order at least one entree. My gf and I only wanted a few drinks and appetizers (we wanted to get three appetizers). When our waiter told us that we'd need to order an entree to sit in the dining area we were both appalled. Mind you, we were already $24 into the meal with their horrible margaritas and almost left the damn place right then and there. We also thought it was silly because we easily would've spent the same amount of money by ordering just appetizers. This left a bad taste in our mouths before eating any food at all. Regardless of our seemingly bad experience, our waiter was professional and mildly helpful most of the time. The rest of the wait staff was also great and attentive to your needs. The building is nicely decorated and much bigger than it looks from the outside. And for what it's worth, the food tasted fresh even if that didn't necessarily make it a good meal. Therefore, only come here if someone else is treating you and you're somehow tired of the other restaurants in the area.

text: We came here during Stone Crab Claw season. It starts Oct 15. They are expensive, around $30.50/lb, but they are good. The claws have some nice, juicy, sweet meat. It's a place to get drunk with your friends at the beach. The decorations are all party-themed and gaudy. Their ceviche comes in a huge cocktail glass. It was very garlicy and nice. I loved the strong flavor of raw garlic inside. Sure, it might not be too traditional, but hey I liked it. The seafood goodies inside was fresh too. I could've done without the potato chips and the corn though. Their chowders can be skipped. They're super thick and clumpy. They seem very sweet and too creamy. It's not smooth or done with any grace. I would avoid. Their original grouper sandwich is huge. It's not a dinky sandwich. It's pretty enormous. It comes with American cheese. I like their fried grouper. They fry it well and the flavor is good. The bun is cheap, supermarket bun. But hey it kinda works. Although for the price, I wished they used something other than cheap super-market type ingredients. Their Fish Tacos are gigantic too. They stuff the hell out of the tortillas. I don't know if you can actually hold it and eat it. You might need to eat it with a fork. They give you two tacos per order, but trust me, they're plenty. Each taco is mini Willy's burritos. Overall, I think they're overpriced. But they have strong drinks and decent food. They have a "fun" atmosphere and the servers are good. I liked it.

Went over all the options and the spec sheet which the salesman said is exactly what we would get in the vehicle we were going to lease and went through the credit process and made a deposit. At one point, the salesman discreetly throws away the original spec sheet and has a new spec sheet with less options for the same price (the good old bait and switch). So then, my boss was pissed off and wanted to cancel the whole thing. This is when the sales manager (Steve Tagye) got involved and to make it up to us, he said he would honor the original spec PLUS add in an upgraded navigation system. So, we mulled about it and decided to do it despite the trickery we encountered. My boss also wanted a hardcover truck bed cover for the vehicle so Mike quoted us $1100 (although not written) and GUARANTEED us that it would be ready for installation come the 1K mile service. Fast forward a month, and we come in for the service and lo and behold the bed cover is not there. Mike visited me in the waiting room and told me that he'll knock off $100 for the cover and ENSURED me that it would be ready within a week. Couple days later, he texts me saying that not only would it take an additional 2-3 weeks, but the sales manager REQUIRED us to pay up front for it and then Mike said it was $1500! (BAIT AND SWITCH AGAIN!) WOW..Sufficed to say, I cancelled the order. I'm not sure if they even put in the order because the guy I am going to to purchase the bed cover said it can be done in a couple days (and much cheaper). All in all, when you go to this dealership, make sure you have your deal in writing as their word is not worth a damn thing. I probably will not do business with this dealership again. I wish Yelp had the option of giving negative stars as this place is probably not worth the 1 star. I do like to note that their service department is pretty good though. text: Who designed this airport?? Serious question. It's pretty terrible. I spent about 5 hours of my life running from gate to gate trying to catch a flight to Buffalo. First off, the gates are numbered weird... I needed gate C25 and I'm walking down the hall and it jumps from C24 to C26. 25 was down a steep ramp and around the corner further down the hall. Why? Just why?? The gates are constantly changing and the people speaking on the intercom talk so fast and incoherent I had to strain to figure out if they were actually speaking English. No seriously. I really was confused. And I speak 3 languages. Hand to God, I missed TWO MORE CONNECTIONS because I'm sitting at the correct gate, on time, waiting to board and the jibber jabber on the intercom was so unintelligible I didn't even realize my flight was boarding. And the flights were small, so before you know it, everyone's checked in and the doors are closed and the plane is gone. No last call, no calling names on the intercom to check if a missing person on the manifest is in the area... I swear it was like little ninjas tiptoed on the plane when no one was looking and took off before you could even turn around. I was dumbfounded. Utterly floored. It happened TWICE. It's not like I've never traveled before! Actually I was already on FOUR international flights just a few weeks before. The third time I was assigned a new flight, I literally stood at the podium, bags in hand, staring the attendant down. I was gonna be the first on that plane damnit!! Also, what the hell is up with Terminal F? You have to get on a shuttle that goes across the tarmac to a different building and it's a real pain in the ass. Especially if you were originally assigned an F gate, then it changed to C and back to F again!! Needless to say, it was the second worst travel fiasco I've ever had to deal with (the first involved a cancelled flight on Christmas Day with an earthquake in Trinidad, but that's another story). My flight back to Florida has to connect in Philly again and I'm already nervous. Pray for me.

text: It is very rare that you get to write a review of an institution that has actually saved your life. At the age of thirteen I was diagnosed with a brain tumor and underwent brain surgery at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The hospital has won many awards and accolades since its establishment, and I personally never received anything but the best of care while a patient. CHOP, as its more commonly known, admits more than 15,000 children each year; if the President's children were sick, they would probably be patients at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. If nothing else, I'm grateful my parents were able to get me the best medical attention possible. There is no doubt in my mind that a lesser hospital, employing less skilled surgeons, would have left me severely brain damaged, or worse. Once arriving at CHOP, my parents, grief-stricken upon learning of my diagnoses, immediately calmed down. The doctors and nurses had a great bedside manner, the perfect mixture of comfort and professionalism. I remember very little from the day of my surgery. An IV was stuck into my arm and an anesthesiologist sedated me. My neurosurgeon was Doctor Suttor, chief of the neurosurgery division at CHOP. I regained consciousness a few hours later, back in my hospital room. The surgery was a success. When I woke back up I wanted nothing more than a cool drink of water. The doctors forbid me from drinking liquids and I had to be content with ice chips. My head pounded and my hair had been shaved during the surgery. There were twenty staples in the back of my head and all of them itched like hell. After the surgery, I couldn't control the entire right side of my body. It was almost as if I had a stroke, except my right arm and leg shook constantly and uncontrollably. There were bed rails on either side of the hospital bed, as if I were a toddler who just graduated from his crib. It's not easy to get much sleep while you're in a hospital. As tired as I was, I couldn't get any rest. During those few times I was able to fall asleep naturally I would soon be woken up. A nurse would barge into my room, stick me with a needle, and shine a light in my eyes. In the days that followed I regained some control over the right side of my body. My limbs still shook constantly, but now I was able do things like hold a pencil or stand up while leaning against something for support. A physical therapist came by one day and I took my first steps outside the hospital room. My tumor was located in the cerebellum--the part of your brain that controls balance and motor skills, among other things. During such an invasive surgery there's bound to be some brain damage. It's no surprise that I was having trouble with walking and coordination. Immediately after the surgery, there was also concern I'd suffer from memory loss--the cerebellum also controls some cognitive functioning, like attention and memory. Fortunately, I was untouched mentally, but trapped inside a body my brain could no longer control. I was only able to walk on my own by using a gait belt to help with balance. Even then, I couldn't take more than ten steps at a time. A doctor came into the hospital room one day and handed me a plastic medical bag. Inside the hermetically sealed bag was the tumor they cut out of my head. My tumor was the size of a golf ball and pink like a wad of bubble gum. It felt empowering to hold in my hand what had once tried to kill me. I was able to hold down Italian water ice, but little else. I remember trying to eat an orange and vomiting all over myself after the first bite. I can't speak to the quality of hospital food, as even the smell turned my stomach. There was a bootlegger outside the hospital who sold VHS copies of movies still in their theatrical run, or not yet released on home video. My parents bought me a few tapes to play on the VCR in my hospital room. I think Titanic was the first movie I watched after the surgery. I could only handle watching television in fifteen-minute increments, so it took a long time before I finished the entire three-hour movie. There was a McDonald's in the basement of CHOP. I never understood why they let the world's unhealthiest fast food restaurant open up a location in a hospital; maybe they thought sick children wouldn't feel so bad if they were eating a happy meal. On my last day in the hospital I ordered a sausage and egg McMuffin with cheese. I ate the breakfast sandwich, a side of hash browns, and was able to keep everything down. It was a personal triumph. If I was able to handle the greasiest food in the world, there was a chance I wouldn't starve and waste away. All told, I spent a total of two weeks in the hospital. I was given the option of staying at CHOP and continuing my physical therapy there, but I opted to go back home and receive treatment at a local facility.

text: Karl and Sarah Worley have taken their biscuits (and more) to a brick-and-mortar Biscuit Love restaurant in the Gulch (next to Bar Louie) with a line out the door! Like any Nashville hot spot, there's a line. We expected as much on Sunday morning, especially given it was CMA Fest weekend! We arrived around 10am I believe, and we were a little nervous about the number of people ahead of us. We were able to browse menus while we waited, as you stay in line as you move inside (and order at the counter) before receiving a number and being loosely directed towards available tables. I feel like we didn't have to wait long at all, because a lot of the groups were large and being a party of three we were ushered forward as tables opened up. The bar is first-come, first-served I believe, but be sure to ask a hostess/server checking on the line! Once we'd ordered, we were served quite quickly! Anna had a Bloody Mary and Dan had a craft beer. I needed caffeine so I had a delicious Arnold Palmer. Anna treated us to my favorite part of the meal... BONUTS. Fried biscuit dough (AMAZING) with sugar, lemon mascarpone, and blueberry compote. I seriously think that when I come back, I will make this my main meal, so I can have them all for myself. My. new. favorite. thing. I had a lot of trouble making up my mind for my main dish, because the menu at the restaurant is much more extensive than the truck's used to be. I decided that for my first visit, I needed to go with my old truck standby, the SEC: biscuit, smoked sausage, egg, and aged cheddar. I had the egg scrambled because I was in the midst of sensory overload when I ordered; I usually prefer the egg fried. But it was delicious nonetheless! Even better than the truck days, honestly... although I wonder if it's because I was eating it in air conditioning at a table with real silverware vs. plastic fork at the market. I also ordered sides of the "chronic" bacon which was sticky and sweet, and the potatoes. The potatoes I wish were a bit crispier, but the bacon was fab. Bacon purists might prefer the normal bacon, but I love a little sweetness with the salt. You guys, do yourself a favor and hit up Biscuit Love... I'm so glad I could take my friend Anna (and Dan, too!) to brunch there, and to meet Karl. I'm so happy for the Worleys and this new adventure, and hoping they put another location in Franklin someday!

Pulled pork was uninspired; a little dry, not much fat, smoke or spice. I am not sure what they were going for. I mean, it was ok, but we'll try the sausage next time. This hash brown is probably one of the best I've ever had. I like this thing better than most places french fries. And the grits, can you say 'cheese'!? text: My wife and I live in Arkansas, but still have Saints' season tickets, so we visit New Orleans pretty often. This past weekend, we brought a friend with us. We drove down on Friday and arrived about 6pm. After dinner at the Palace Cafe (subject of another review) we ended up at Razzoo's on Bourbon St. Good music, drinks, fun. They have a stage with live entertainment, several bars, an outdoor patio, plenty of bathrooms, and even when the place is crowded, you don't feel jammed in. This recent trip turned out to be very special, as you will understand if you read the rest of my review. Not long after we arrived, a friend in our party got her wallet picked out of her purse. (It was unzipped.) She noticed it immediately after, and we notified one of the security guys at the door. Within seconds, there were multiple employees around, including the manager on duty, asking questions. They went and checked the security video, and got perfect images of the two thieves. Several of the security guys spread into the French Quarter while one of them took a copy of the video to the local police precinct two blocks away. My wife and I accompanied our friend to the police station to file a police report, but not really expecting that much would result from it. Were we wrong. Within two hours of the theft, the two culprits were arrested by a Louisiana state trooper. One of Razzoo's security guys was combing the Quarter, came across the perps with another mark, and grabbed a trooper who was assigned to that street. The two were arrested without a problem. A search turned up nothing but a couple of hundred dollars in cash. The manager on duty was named Reuben, and he told us that Razzoo's had recently put in a new security camera system. After the state trooper showed us his copy of the video, it was obvious that the investment by the club was worth the money. The clarity of the picture was perfect and it identified the thieves without question. Turned out that one of the arrested pickpockets had just been paroled from prison the day before after serving 25 years of a 40-year sentence for murder. (!) So much for that early release. We will go to Razzoo's more often after this experience. Part 2 - The next morning, our friend got a call from a woman from Florida who had found her personal effects in an alley where the thieves discarded them after the crime. She had googled our friend's name, found her on LinkedIn, saw her resume online that included the phone number and called. (The wonders of modern technology.) We met with the woman and her husband later that day, and our friend got her driver's license, credit cards, personal papers, etc all returned to her. (I have to admit that if I hadn't seen all this with my own eyes, I never would have believed that this kind of outcome was possible.) Thank you, Razzoo's for reminding us that there are more good people in our society than bad. Note: The club is undergoing renovations on their patio area this week and announced that they would be closed for a few days while this work is going on. If you walk by and they're open, go.

The owner is a New York native, moved to Philly and opened this restaurant 3 years ago. All of the staff were really truly very nice and professional. We ordered 4 small plates and shared 1 dessert. The kitchen gave us 2 complimentary appetizers (potato soup with parsley oil, tuna tartare with crushed rice crackers), which were really nice. I have to mention that the sourdough toast they sell for only $1 is very good as well. Maryland Crab on toast: the owner Ms. Vernick recommended it. Lump crab meat spread generously on toasts. Light and delicious. The special pasta of the day: Tagliatelle tossed in light sauce with sausage and red currants. The combination of savory sausage and sweet currants was amazing. My boyfriend loves more tender pasta, and it was cooked just right for him. Arctic Char, Crispy Skin & Dill: The fish was carefully prepared. Just fish, non-greasy crispy skin and bits of dill, but it leaves a very fresh feeling in your mouth. Grilled Heart of Romaine, Figs, Aged Cheddar: This might have been the best grilled romaine I have ever had, just as when I was more than ready to forget this dish for good. The romaine is warm on the outside, very juicy and crisp inside. Just a little too salty on the soft leaves, but not bad enough for me to take one star off. The addition of figs stuffed in the romaine is unforgettably tasty. The Date Cake: A nice portion for two people to share. Not too sweet yet so satisfying! I only wish I didn't manage to stop myself from getting the last bite... Also, as we were sitting by the kitchen, I was watching the kitchen staff and food runners closely. They were very serious about making food - the chef reads a timer for every dish, and the food runners were always waiting at the counter. The guy at the back was spending 2 minutes on cleaning one single glass, literally. We never heard chitchat during the course of our dinner. These are serious food lovers/makers, which explains why Vernick has received many compliments on Yelp. Can't wait to come back!

text: Background: I grew up in CA eating tacos and burritos from local taquerias from SD to SF until a few years ago. The guacamole has no pico in it, and thus little flavor. The pastor isn't sweet and savory and is missing the hot piña slice (common in Florida for some reason). The chorizo is chunky and not smooth. Ricos/street tacos are called "TJ tacos". You can't mix and match these tacos which makes no sense. The price is too high for what you get ($2+ for a fountain drink). They should get 3 stars for these obvious heretical transgressions. That said, the pico is baller; the hot sauce is baller, the carnitas are baller, the asada is baller. The tacos are too big but they are borderline baller. The Godzilla burrito will slay a donkey. And, most importantly, there just aren't any places doing it better unless you sit down. So I am begrudgingly giving it a 4-stars. I've eaten here 4 times in 3 weeks. The hot sauce is what's doing it for me, it's what I want from my taco place.

For me, personally, I knew something was off when I ordered a diet coke with lime...and it came out a diet coke with lemon (granted, this by itself is a small deal). But the cold beans and rice was a first for me...and I've eaten out hundreds of times at mexican restaurants in the Nashville area the past 6-7 years. On top of this, there was no offer of a partial refund on any part of our order to account for the multiple mishaps. So, that was additional salt on the wound. Overall, the taste was medicore...definitely not anything special to justify the poor service. The prices are fair, but still...I have no clue why the ratings are so high with this place. text: Sadly, I am removing my previous, very positive review of El Sarape and replacing it with this one, which is the opposite: completely negative. And yet the food is still great, the wait staff still welcoming and highly competent. So what changed my opinion? One awful experience. And that is the lesson I'm trying to convey: One bad experience can outweigh many good ones. The tale begins with a Groupon we had not been able to use, and which was expiring that day. We called, made a reservation, telling them we had a Groupon that we had just remembered we had. The only table open was just barely doable for us, time-wise, if we rushed, so we left immediately. When we arrived, we once again told them we had a Groupon. When we ordered, we repeated that we had a Groupon, since restaurants always want to be told them about it in advance of ordering. The meal was good. We had bought the Groupon intending to use it with friends (the reason we did not use the Groupon earlier or invite friends to join us comes later in this review), so we ordered more food than we needed in order to use its value. We gave the Groupon to the waitress; after a few minutes she returned and told us they couldn't take it because it was Saturday night and it was only valid from Sunday through Thursday. So there we were, faced with a very large check we had not expected. And this is exactly the situation that every restaurant should try to avoid. No one likes surprises when it comes to money. Noticing the manager, I got up and told her our problem and asked why no one had told us--considering that they had three opportunities to do so--that our Groupon was not valid. She told me there are all sorts of Groupon offers and that "this happens all the time." I noted that the very fact that it "happens all the time" should motivate her to have her staff ask to see the Groupon before people order their food. I mentioned that no one likes to be surprised about money. Most regrettably, the manager actually laughed out loud at my suggestion. I went and sat down, having just been humiliated in front of many people. It got worse--she watched me sit down, made eye contact, and once again snickered, no doubt pleased that she had forced this nasty woman who was obviously trying to pull a fast one to pay her a lot of money. The laughing at me part motivated my husband to go speak to the manager. I should here mention that the reason we had not used the Groupon previously was that he'd had a heart attack. This was the first time since leaving the hospital we had gone out; we were trying to have a quiet dinner to celebrate the fact that he was alive. Yes, it was on us to have checked the Groupon more closely. But sometimes the reasons people do dumb things is not that they are stupid or dishonest. Sometimes they have a lot of more important things on their minds. The hospitality business is about knowing that, not about shaming people, laughing at them or insulting them. Yet not at El Sarape! Oh my no! The manager was just as rude to my husband as she'd been to me. She asked him what he wanted her to do. He told her he wanted her to honor the Groupon. She told him not to tell her how to run her business. Seriously, those are her exact words, after specifically asking him what he wanted her to do! I have never experienced quite that level of arrogance in a restaurant. The manager did grudgingly give us a gift card, but didn't tell us how much it's worth. Frankly, I expect it has $5.00 on it, but even if it was $5,000.00 we will not be returning to any of the Sarape restaurants (El Sarape and the two Los Sarapes, all owned by the same people). Ever.

text: Writing a bad review is tough as you don't want to come off as jilted or overly negative but in our case we felt, that after working with PtoP on resolution, we needed to share our experience with everyone we can. We used PtoP based on the recommendation of our agent. They liked that it was a "one stop shop" for all the inspections rather than having to schedule each one separately and also liked that the report is generated on site rather than having to wait. We felt the price of the inspection was a little high but did appreciate the convenience and turn around time so went forward with them. On the day of inspection we met the inspector and another guy that I believe was in training. At the same time we had the other inspectors showing up as well. Overall, it was a typical inspection where they'd call out anything specific they wanted us to review. Overall they noted nothing major other than some water coming in around the existing roof penetrations. There were a handful of other cosmetic/best practice recommendations. The report had a section at the front for the items that needed addressed and we reviewed those that morning after they were done. Overall, it was a smooth transaction and inspection (other than a snafu with the sewer inspection but that wasn't PtoP's issue). The guys were very friendly and it was a nice morning process. After moving in though we started finding things they didn't: - The biggest item of concern is we found that significant wood rot was found on a sun-room that we'll either have to totally rip off or invest significantly to repair. Detailed below. - We noticed that the showers weren't inspected. One drain still had a layer of dirt/dust so we know they didn't run the shower to test it otherwise it'd have been rinsed. The drain in the master bath filled with water the first time we took a shower as it was nearly plugged so clearly they didn't test that either otherwise we'd expect the report to suggest service on the drain. - The exhaust fans in the same two bathrooms were unplugged in the ceiling. Not a big deal but clearly not tested so if they didn't work we'd have not caught it before the purchase. - The more detailed report (not reviewed on site) said the attic space wasn't inspected b/c it would be dangerous. The attic is fully lit and has plywood from wall to wall so you can walk through it. - We have a full 4" or bigger hole on the side of the house from an unused stove vent. Only thing on the report was a small note about filling hole penetrations around wires. I spoke with the owner of the PtoP franchise and he was very very good to work with. I stress that - very professional and courteous. He asked that i let the previous inspector come back out to document the miss. Several weeks later I met him and he reviewed the rotted area (as that was the primary concern). Note we've since found another rotted section but at the time only one was being discussed. Again the inspector was nice but his position was that if the sellers were hiding it they can't be expected to find it. I called out the other missed items that were basic drawing attention to the lack of detail and focus on our inspection. I also called out that I, a casual home owner and not a professional inspector, found the rotted section just by happenstance and noted the un-hidden water damage signs around the problem. That generally ended the conversation and it was back to the franchise owner for next steps. End result was a full refund of the inspection. But, and this is what bothers me, the criteria for a refund was that I waive ALL liability for future claims due to the missed inspection items. Repair of the single section is north of $5k without accounting for window replacement. Now we're looking at the other section as well that's rotted out on a different wall. So the Sunroom as a whole is facing $10k in repairs. Easily something that could have been negotiated out during the home purchase. I don't expect PtoP to be accountable for the loss of value and cost of full repair, but I do think it's bad business for them to hold a refund hostage pending a release of liability. It really looks like they too are worried they missed other major items on our house. Very long story short - They don't stand behind their inspection clearly by asking that we release them of liability to refund the purchase price.

text: Oh Pho, how I love thee. That being said, I've had my share of this Vietnamese bowl of deliciousness around Philly and up and down the East Coast. Unfortunately, my hometown city always came up a bit short. There are great Vietnamese restaurants here, but I've never been wowed by their pho. Enter Saigon Cuisine. Tucked on the corner of 40th Street where University City and West Philly meet is this small gem. Hell, it's directly next to an equally small Indian and Thai restaurant. So at quick glance you may lose it in the shuffle. But it's there, and it's worth the look. The outside, I'll admit, may throw you. The sign is a bit dingy, there's an empty lot half a block down, can't see inside to even see of the place is open. But. Once you step in all if your fears are put away Inside is bright with bamboo floor (I think) with red booths and tables, modern pop music playing in the background and a single TV on mute with what looks to be a Vietnamese news station. Oh, and the smell. You'd live in a dumpster if it smelled like this restaurant. I got here on a Monday at Noon with a friend and we were seated promptly. Plenty of booths and had an ok crowd. Maybe about 1/3 full. Our waitress immediately took got us water and handed menus. The menu here is small but gets the point across. I ordered the brisket pho (large) and steamed pork dumplings. While my friend ordered beef eye pho and summer rolls. The food (minus my dumplings) were out in no time. Which tells me they have this stuff at the ready. Good move, ownership. The summer rolls we're bulky, full of greens and shrimp and came with a sweet peanut sauce for dipping. My dumplings came out fresh, hot, and with a little sear on them from the grill. Also with a dipping sauce. And once they were cooled I couldn't keep them out of my mouth. So sad when I had gone through my serving of 5. Now the pho. Our waitress started by bringing out a plate of bean sprouts, jalapeños, sliced limes and a bottle of soy sauce. I was super excited when I saw that huge bowl coming my way. I could smell the spices before our waitress even put them down. The bowl was pretty big. Definitely a large bowl if there ever was one. The meat was tender in sliced pieces making them flavorful and easy to eat, the noodles were cooked to perfection. The broth at the end was so good I had to forego the spoon and drink it from the bowl. So, needless to say I am a fan if this small slice of pho heaven. The only reason it's 4/5 stars is the wait staff. I get it was a slow lunch rush and there weren't many people in but to see the entire staff with their noses buried in their phones within view of the customers was a bit off putting. I don't wanna bash too hard. Because when it was game time our waitress came ready to play. We didn't wait too long for food or refills or anything. I guess it just seemed unprofessional to see them all in the phone. But other than that, they were great. I'll definitely be dining here again when I need a pho fix.

text: Great restaurant, fun vibe and creative thoughtful menu. I have been here a few times now and after reading several of the reviews, especially from those who have only been there once, I am amazed at how critical people can be. The atmosphere is a bit on the loud side, but what do you expect when your in a fun open setting. That makes it all the more interesting. If I wanted quiet, I would have stayed home. The booths are my favorite, big and comfortable with enough space for a large party and still with elbow room to eat. Our booth was an awesome spot to do the south tampa people watch, and what a scene it is! Loved that I could meld into the beautiful woodwork and enjoy. Our dinner was exceptionally enjoyable from the time the host greeted us to when our waiter wished a safe ride home. Stating with the wines by the glass, smart to have Italian choices. I tend to be a creature of habit so to not sway too far off my normal Sonoma Chardonnay they offered me a delicious Il Borro white. Smooth and refreshing, loved it. Also the wine glasses themselves have a clever design that allows each glass to breath. I thought there was a crack in the glass but when the owner stopped by to say hello, he explained how they work and swirled my husbands red. The attention to detail is truly amazing and I haven't even gotten to the food. We had the luxury of asking the owner bit more about the menu and he went on to share with us how each morning the bread is kneaded and baked in the wood oven, and that each of the cavatelli pastas are hand rolled. Reminded me of my great Italian aunts' pasta dishes. I had to order both! And I wasn't disappointed, it brought me back. The pasta was tender and flavorful and the sauce was fresh and simple. Not overbearing and heavy. The perfect balance and the right amount. So tired of the large oversized portions. The table also ordered the muscles with more of the scrumptious bread. While I am not a muscles person, I could have devoured the sauce by myself. Along with the smokey flavor of the bread dipped in the sauce, the combination was heaven. Another guest with us had the Kale Salad and the meatballs. Wow another great combo choice. Love the Kale in the tempura batter, crispy, tangy and spectacular. And the meatballs, something I have been known to make mean one myself, were presented by themselves with no sauce. Very daring since a meatball without sauce better be pretty darn good. Again they were flavorful, and spices used were the right amount to complement the meat. Our daughter ordered the margherita pizza and loved the flavor of the crust but would have liked a bit more cheese. (and what kid wouldn't like more). Anyway it was definitely reminiscent of the pizzas we had in Italy, so again kudos to the authenticity of everything Ava's is doing. Yes I'm a fan! See you at Ava's soon.

We started off with Bruschetta as our opener, which was an absolute delight. There were so many flavors combined together that just made it PERFECT, in my opinion. As for our entrees, I would have to say they were "so-so", especially for the price you're paying. The presentation was great, as well as the proportions, but I feel they were lacking seasoning for they were a little on the bland side. My husband ordered the pan-seared duck, which was good, but not great. In my opinion, it could have been more flavorful. As for my entree, I ordered the vegan sweet potato gnocchi (I also added chicken & parmesan to it, since I'm not vegan). This dish also came with a good proportion, but was also on the bland side. For our dessert, we ordered the triple chocolate cake, and OMG this is to DIE for! We didn't want to get too stuffed, so we didn't make it an "a la mode" (which I slightly regret now), but it was delicious as is. It is an absolute MUST TRY. Overall, if I could, I would rate this review with 3.5 stars, just because I feel as if they still need time to tweak the menu/recipes a slight bit more and also straighten up their staff slightly (we couldn't even find our waitress a few times and sat with empty drinks). They are a new restaurant, so I definitely would not hold it against them for now. I would still recommend this spot to everyone to try. I think it would be the best place to swing by during lunch to stop for a couple drinks and snack on openers for sure. As for myself, I'll give them some time until I come back for their entrees, but I will definitely be back for their drinks and their openers/desserts.

text: My hubby and I heard about Carsense through a friend who highly recommended the place since he bought his last two cars from them. It was our first time shopping and we didn't really know what size vehicle we wanted so we were just looking. We decided on a Town and Country but I needed a special pedal adjustment that's not listed as an option in any vehicle states so tony looked through a lot of van pictures with us to pick out several with this option. He was very friendly and made sure to ask if we wanted anything, ( They have a free and nicely set up drink station with soda, juice, hot tea, hot coco...ect.) We finally narrowed it down to two vans and I became very incisive. I changed my mind twice. Tony was as I said very patient and kind and didn't make me feel pressured at all. Btw, they get paid the same commission no matter what vehicle they sell you, so there is no pressure from them to spend more. The van I chose was at another Carsense so we had to come back. We made an appointment and when we got there it was pouring rain. Tony met us at the door with a big smile and asked if we wanted anything to drink. We did the online finance approval on their website between visits (Highly recommend-speeds up the process). Tony had everything ready for us and walked us through the add on protection they offer. Btw, they have a life time guarantee on the engine life, and a 5 day return policy- which Carmax only has the return policy. Everything went smoothly and quickly. We test drove the van in the rain and noticed spots from maybe a wax on the windshield that made it hard to see. Tony took the van to the service department immediately. They couldn't fix it that night so they gave us an I owe you for the repairs ( only at night in the rain could you even see the spots). After the official purchase of the van Tony met us outside (it had stopped raining thank God) and Sam walked us through all the features of the van to show us how everything worked, we needed it, Thank you Sam! I made an appointment online for the service and within a hour got an email saying my appointment was confirmed. I came in for my appointment and was met with Scott over at the service station. They confirmed all my info and asked me to wait in the waiting room. It had comfy couches, chairs, and a drink bar, and tv. I didn't wait long and Scott came in and said they couldn't' repair the windshield so they would replace it at no cost to me. They couldn't get the windshield until the next day so Tony got me a loaner car, a ford escape with a sun roof and all the bells and whistles my van has. Tony had previously asked me to let him know when my appointment was so he could have a car ready for me. Well I forgot to tell him... Sorry Tony! He was again so kind and even though he was busy he managed to quickly get a car ready for me. He handed me off to Jim because Tony was with a costumer. Jim was nice enough to fill out the couple pieces of paperwork and then show me the vehicle and how to operate the basics of the SUV. All in all I would highly recommend the people at Carsense to anyone looking to buy a vehicle. Large selection, the atmosphere is relaxing and everyone is really friendly. Btw, we did end up going to Carmax between visits to Carsense. We felt pressured to buy there, and they offered me less for my trade in. Also the vehicle we test drove wasn't cleaned very well. Another difference is Carsense gives you the keys for a test drive and says go have fun, while Carmax has their sales guy go with you and tells you where to drive and tries to sell you the vehicle the whole time. Again felt very pressured to buy something at Carmax. Go to Carsense and asked for tony, tell him I sent you it will make him smile even more.
